title: Quantitative assessment of glycolysis in Crabtree-positive yeasts using stable isotope tracing
author: Niphadkar, Sreedharan, et al.

steps.title: Prepare yeast growth media
steps.instruction: Weigh yeast extract and peptone for the desired final volume, dissolve in distilled water, autoclave at 121 °C for 30 min, cool, add filter‑sterilized glucose to a final concentration of 2 % (use 1 % glucose for shifting cells), aliquot 16 mL of YP (2 % glucose) into labeled conical flasks for starter cultures, and label 50 mL conical tubes and 1.5 mL vials for shifting cells.

steps.title: Prepare quenching and extraction buffers
steps.instruction: Make 60 % (v/v) methanol quenching buffer (≈1 L) by mixing methanol with distilled water; store at –20 °C. Make 75 % (v/v) ethanol extraction buffer (≈40 mL) by mixing MS‑grade ethanol with LC‑MS‑grade water; prepare fresh before extraction and keep at room temperature. Label the required number of 50 mL conical tubes and 2 mL microcentrifuge vials for extraction, aliquot 40 mL chilled quenching buffer into the conical tubes, and pre‑chill these tubes at –40 °C in a dewar containing 60 % methanol (maintain –40 °C to –45 °C, never below –50 °C). Keep centrifuges at –5 °C and a heating block at 80 °C. Prepare a 50 % (w/v) ¹³C₆‑glucose solution by weighing 2 g ¹³C₆‑glucose and dissolving in distilled water to a final volume of ≈4 mL; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Label cells and extract metabolites
steps.instruction: To each tube containing ~5 OD₆₀₀ log‑phase cells, add freshly prepared ¹³C₆‑glucose to a final concentration of 1 % (≈100 µL for 5 mL of 5 OD₆₀₀ cells), giving a total glucose concentration of 2 % (1 % unlabeled + 1 % labeled). Manually shake the tubes and immediately add 40 mL chilled quenching buffer (maintained at –40 °C). For short time points (3, 10, 30 s) use a timer to shake and add buffer at the exact intervals; for longer time points (≥1 min) keep shaking after glucose addition, then quickly add chilled buffer at the desired times. Keep the tubes in the –40 °C dewar for 5 min, then centrifuge at 1000 × g for 3 min at –5 °C. Decant supernatant, add 1 mL chilled quenching buffer, resuspend the pellet by pipetting, and transfer the suspension to a 2 mL tube. Centrifuge the 2 mL tubes at 1000 × g for 2 min at –5 °C and discard supernatant. Add 1 mL extraction buffer (75 % ethanol) to the pellet, vortex ≈20 s, heat at 80 °C for 3 min, then place on ice for 5 min. Spin at 20 000 × g for 1 min at room temperature, transfer 950 µL supernatant to a fresh 1.5 mL tube, spin again at 20 000 × g for 10 min at room temperature, and transfer 900 µL supernatant to a new tube. Optionally divide the extract into three fractions for later derivatization. Dry the samples in a vacuum concentrator. Samples may be stored at –80 °C for a few weeks, but TCA‑cycle metabolites (aspartate, malate, fumarate) should be derivatized immediately for accurate quantitation.

steps.title: Derivatize TCA metabolites
steps.instruction: Dissolve the dried metabolite extract in 50 µL LC‑MS‑grade water, add 50 µL of 1 M 1‑ethyl‑3‑(3‑dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide (EDC) and shake for 10 min at room temperature. Add 100 µL of 0.5 M O‑benzylhydroxylamine (OBHA) and shake on a mixer for 1 h. Add 300 µL ethyl acetate, shake for 10 min, then transfer the top organic layer to a fresh tube. Repeat the OBHA addition (step above) two more times, each followed by ethyl acetate extraction, and pool all top layers. Dry the pooled, derivatized extract using a vacuum concentrator. The derivatized samples can be stored at –80 °C until LC‑MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: Perform LC‑MS/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Before running samples, inject several blanks (LC‑MS‑grade water) and a standard containing all target metabolites to check background and peak quality. For non‑derivatized samples, dissolve in 1 mL water; for derivatized samples, dissolve in 1 mL 1:1 water:methanol. Inject an appropriate volume onto a Synergi Fusion‑RP column (80 Å, 150 × 4.6 mm) on a Shimadzu Nexera HPLC. For non‑derivatized metabolites use buffer A′ (5 mM ammonium acetate in H₂O) and buffer B′ (100 % acetonitrile); detect glycolysis and PPP intermediates in negative polarity mode. For derivatized (and amino acid/nucleotide) samples use buffer A (99.9 % H₂O + 0.1 % formic acid) and buffer B (99.9 % methanol + 0.1 % formic acid); detect amino acids, nucleotides, and OBHA‑derivatized TCA metabolites in positive polarity mode. Use an AB Sciex 5500 (or 6500) triple‑quadrupole mass spectrometer in MRM mode to measure steady‑state and labeled metabolite amounts.

steps.title: Analyze LC‑MS/MS data
steps.instruction: Import the raw data into MultiQuant software. Create a quantitation method using the standard data: set retention times based on unlabeled metabolites and define integration parameters (Gaussian smooth width = 2, RT half‑window = 30 s, minimum peak width = 3 points, minimum peak height = 0, noise = 75 %, baseline subtraction window = 2 min, report largest peak = yes). Apply this method to all sample files, manually adjusting peak integration where necessary. Calculate the area under the curve for each labeled and unlabeled metabolite, then compute percent labeling as (intensity of the specific labeled mass) / (total intensity of all detected isotopologues for that metabolite).
